newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn sells 9.8 bln dmk 10-yr bond, 101.31 and over.
newsitem.headline: Bonn sells 9.8 bln dmk 10-yr bond, 101.31 and over.

text.p: The German government on Tuesday topped up its six percent, 10-year New Year Bond maturing on January 4, 2007 by allocating 9.8 billion marks of the paper in an auction at a price of 101.31 and above, the Bundesbank as issuing agent said.
The weighted average price was 101.36 and the average yield was 5.81 percent, the Bundesbank said.

The Bundesbank said it was retaining 2.2 billion marks of the issue for market-smoothing purposes, bringing the total volume of the top-up to 12 billion marks and raising the overall volume of the New Year Bond to 27 billion marks.
Bids for the top-up totalled 19.77 billion marks. All bids at the lowest rate were accepted. A total of 50 percent of bids which did not specify a price were accepted.
The settlement date on the additional tranche is January 30 and the portion will be included in the stock exchange listing on January 31, the Bundesbank said.
Only members of the Federal Bond Consortium were allowed to participate directly in the auction. The bond carries the securities number 113502.
